summary: Assist customer with safe revert and guardrails after applying quantization + batching + cache tuning
description:
Issue summary: Customer LexaForms applied a combined optimization profile (q4f16 quantization, increased dynamic batch_size to 256, and aggressive KV prefix caching TTL=30s) to their Dedicated pool last night. After the change they report increased hallucination rate on rw-chat-lg-1 and a spike in tail latency for long-response (>512 tokens) requests. They want step-by-step assistance to safely revert or adjust config without downtime and to introduce guardrails for future tune-ups.

Impact: User-visible quality regressions and tail latency spikes impacting 2 services: chatbot and document summarization. Traffic is routed through their dedicated pool in us-east with occasional failover to eu-west. Estimated affected traffic: ~12% of requests (higher for long-form endpoints).

Environment: dedicated prod pool (lexaforms-dedicated-us-east). Redwood Console traces and latency SLOs attached.

Initial hypothesis: The q4f16 profile likely reduced numeric fidelity on specific attention heads causing token-level degeneration in rw-chat-lg-1; increased batching raised per-request scheduling latency under high concurrency (long tail due to mixed short/long seqs); aggressive prefix cache TTL caused cache churn and frequent KV cache miss amplification under traffic patterns with many distinct prefixes (multi-turn sessions). The combination amplified tail effects and exposed model sensitivity to lower-precision arithmetic.

What customer has tried: They rolled the profile live at 2026-03-12T22:45Z, monitored for 40 minutes, then observed issues and patched batch_size back to 64 in the console at 2026-03-12T23:35Z. They did NOT revert quantization or cache TTL. No infra or node changes were made.

Requested outcome: 1) A short safe revert plan that minimizes downtime, 2) A checklist for canary testing future optimization changes, 3) Concrete config suggestions (quant, batch, caching) tuned for rw-chat-lg-1 and how to codify guardrails in Console.

Attachments/Links: Console traces: https://console.redwood.ai/lexaforms/traces/incident-11827, latency heatmap: https://console.redwood.ai/lexaforms/heatmaps/11827, slack thread: #support-lexaforms (https://slack.redwood.ai/archives/C05XXXXXX), relevant PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/3421

Suggested safe revert plan (short):
1) Enter maintenance mode for the dedicated pool in Console (non-disruptive routing: set drain=false and reduce new-session percentage to 10% to limit blast radius).
2) Create a canary route: duplicate current route and pin to previous model variant (rw-chat-lg-1@v1.13) without q4f16 quant. Target 5% of production traffic for 15 minutes.
3) If canary passes (no hallucinations, tail latency within baseline), promote previous model variant to 30% for 30 minutes.
4) Revert cache TTL to conservative value (300s) on the canary and measure KV hit-rate and downstream tail latency.
5) If stable, roll back quantization to v1.13 across pool during a low-traffic window with staged increments (30% -> 60% -> 100%).
6) Once reverted, restore batch_size policy to adaptive mode (max_batch=128, max_concurrency=8) and enable per-route batching thresholds based on median sequence length.

Quick verification checks (what to watch during canary):
- End-to-end latency p50/p95/p99 for the route and distribution across sequence lengths.
- Token-level log sampling for hallucination signals (flapping facts, low-confidence tokens).
- KV cache hit rate and cache fill churn rate.
- Serving runtime errors / NaN/overflow events.
- Heap/GPU utilization and scheduling queue lengths.

Backout commands / Console actions (examples):
- Re-pin model variant: `redwood route update --route-id lr-chat-main --model rw-chat-lg-1@v1.13`
- Set cache TTL: `redwood pool update --pool lexaforms-dedicated-us-east --cache-ttl 300`
- Adjust batching policy: `redwood config set --route lr-chat-main batching.max_batch=128 batching.max_concurrency=8`

Longer-term guardrails to implement (recommendations):
1) Always run combined-change canary: never change quantization + batching + cache at the same time. Split into sequential canaries and keep one axis constant.
2) Add automatic model-quality hooks: baseline token-level metrics (per-prompt test suite) that fail deployments if KL divergence or F1 drift exceeds threshold.
3) Add preflight synthetic load tests for mixed short/long seq distributions using the customer's traffic replay (stored in S3).
4) Require a rollback playbook attached to any Optimize profile that changes both precision and batching.
5) Console policy: disallow q4f* quant profiles on rw-chat-lg-1 unless explicitly whitelisted for the customer pool.

Follow-ups requested from Engineering (recommended):
- Run a focused eval of q4f16 on rw-chat-lg-1 using customer prompt set (assigned to Applied ML) and share a small report.
- Add a dashboard tile showing KV cache miss amplification (per-prefix miss rate) and correlate it with tail latency.

Resolution target: Provide step-by-step assist today, complete canary, and schedule follow-up for hardening in 72 hours.

resolution: In Progress - canary showing positive results. Recommended full revert of q4f16 across pool in staged rollout pending Applied ML eval. Customer to confirm low-traffic window for final rollback.
